title: Pricing Desk Note: Financing the Upfront Program Fee into the Mortgage Loan File Loan Amount
content:
Where a Mortgage Loan File's program carries an upfront program fee (the FHA upfront mortgage insurance premium or the VA funding fee), the fee is financed: the loan amount equals the base loan amount plus the base loan amount multiplied by the program's upfront program fee percentage, rounded to the cent. A VA borrower who is exempt from the funding fee (a veteran receiving VA service-connected disability compensation) pays no funding fee, and the loan amount equals the base loan amount. Programs whose upfront program fee is 0.000 percent always carry a loan amount equal to the base loan amount. Program limits are tested on the base loan amount, never on the financed total. Whenever the base loan amount or the program changes, the loan amount is recomputed in the same update.

## Worked figures (hypothetical base loan amounts)

| Program | Base loan amount | Upfront rate | Loan amount |
|---|---|---|---|
| Larkspur FHA 30-Year Fixed | 250000.00 USD | 1.750% | 250000.00 plus 4375.00, which is 254375.00 USD |
| Larkspur VA 30-Year Fixed, not exempt | 312345.00 USD | 2.150% | 312345.00 plus 6715.4175, which is 319060.4175, rounded to 319060.42 USD |
| Larkspur VA 30-Year Fixed, exempt veteran | 312345.00 USD | none paid | 312345.00 USD |
| Larkspur Conventional 30-Year Fixed | 312345.00 USD | 0.000% | 312345.00 USD |

## Points of judgement

- **Which amount is tested against the program's maximum loan amount?** The base loan amount. A hypothetical Larkspur FHA 30-Year Fixed base loan amount at the program maximum stays eligible even though the financed loan amount is higher.
- **When is the loan amount recomputed?** In the same update in which the base loan amount or the program changes.
